label: Bible Study
prompt: And he shall be like a _____ planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
verse: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
note: The very first psalm sketches the righteous as a riverside tree — Jeremiah borrows the picture later.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the _____ works of God.
verse: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
note: Elihu's advice to weary Job: stand still and consider the wondrous works of God — sometimes just look up.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in _____, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
verse: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
note: The KJV spells it 'morter' — Israel's lives made bitter with brick and mortar under Egypt's taskmasters.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a _____ of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
verse: And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
note: Achor means 'trouble' — the valley where Achan was judged becomes a doorway of hope.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it _____ me nothing.
verse: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.
note: Even giving everything away, even martyrdom, without love adds up to zero: 'it profiteth me nothing.'
